Waiting for the team's response to my unavailability.

I don't want to look uncooperative, but I'm at my limit.
Waiting to see who will propose a plan.

My section still needs a lot of work. And I don't know how to do that analysis.
I've stated my position and limitations. Waiting for others to respond.

I can walk someone through the rest of it before I have to leave.
Waiting to see if they accept my offer to explain my work.

I've proposed a solution. Now I'm waiting for Farah's response.

I can't, Hafiz. I'm already covering for the colleague who's on leave.
I've explained my position and now I'm waiting for a response.

It's the best option we have right now.
Okay. What if I take over the work you're covering? All of it. That would free you up completely for Sarah's section. Can that work?
I've made a more concrete offer to Farah. I'm waiting for her response.

Waiting to hear Farah's response to Hafiz's offer.

Waiting for Hafiz and Farah to agree on a plan to cover my work.

STRATEGY: COUNTER_PROPOSE. Farah's objection is reasonable; she's already overloaded. My last offer was too vague. I need to remove her obstacle entirely. Okay. What if I take over the work you're covering? All of it. That would free you up completely for Sarah's section. Can that work?
I've made a concrete proposal to clear Farah's plate. Now I need her answer.

A flat 'no' seems uncooperative now that he's offered to take all my other work. Maybe we can split Sarah's section instead of just shifting the entire burden to me.
That's a lot for you to take on. But Sarah's section is the analysis... it's not something I can just pick up. What if we split her section?
I've made a counter-proposal to split the work.

STRATEGY: COUNTER_PROPOSE. Farah's suggesting we split the section. That sounds inefficient. We don't have time for hand-offs between two people on one section. It's better if one person owns it, especially since Sarah can do a single, focused handover before she leaves. Splitting it doesn't solve the problem that the work is hard; it just creates more coordination problems. I need to explain this and push for one person to take it.
I think splitting it will be slower. We need one person to own it. Sarah can give you a full handover before she leaves. That's our best shot to get it done right.
I've explained why splitting the work is a bad idea and restated my proposed path forward. Waiting for Farah's response.

Hafiz is pushing for one person to take over Sarah's work, and he's right that splitting it could be messy and slow. It's better if they sort this out between them. As long as I don't have to do it, I'm fine. I'll just stay quiet.

Hafiz is pushing his idea for Farah to take my section. He's counting on me to do a handover, which I offered. Farah still sounds like she's not sure she can do the analysis. Splitting work creates coordination overhead we don't have time for.

I've addressed Farah's concerns and reinforced my position. Now I'm waiting for her to respond.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Farah is still arguing to split the work, now calling it a risk-management issue. I see the opposite. Hafiz is really pushing this. He's not giving Farah any room to disagree. As long as they're focused on each other, they're not looking at me. It's better for me to just stay quiet. I've already said I can't do it. Getting involved now would be a mistake.

Hafiz is really pushing Farah to take my work. She sounds worried about the analysis, but he's not really hearing that. This is awkward, they're arguing about how to cover for me. Two people working on it is safer, even if it requires a bit of coordination.

STRATEGY: ASSERT. Sarah needs to leave now. This entire argument is wasting what little time we have for the handover. Her urgency is the final word. I need to end this debate and get Farah to start the handover immediately. It's my call as lead.
